lines.note: Hikichirasu is scattering or spreading out. The headword starts this leaf and confirms that the preceding Fiqi is a catchword.

runs.text: gũa couſa eſtendida como em prato, bande-

lines.note: The thing is spread across a plate or tray. Both algũa and bandeja are divided across physical lines without changing the sentence structure.
Ja finishes bandeja, tray; this short fragment belongs to the gloss rather than Japanese ja.
Hikikomoru is withdrawing or remaining shut in. Recolher-se gives the first equivalent and es- begins estar.
Estar encerrado completes being enclosed or secluded. It is the second Portuguese equivalent of hikikomoru.

runs.text: Couſa que ſe alega como exemplo,

lines.note: Hikikoto is something adduced as an example, connecting hiku's citation sense with koto.
A story is another example of what may be cited. Historia remains within the same gloss.
Hikikosu is pulling timber over an obstruction. Its oita past is preserved rather than regularized from modern morphology.

runs.text: paſſar monte, ou outro lugar alto, &c. ¶ Itẽ,

lines.note: The obstruction can be a mountain or high place. The second tall-looking type in paſſar is not an l forming palſar.

runs.text: Deſaparecerem as aues quando as ſeguem por

lines.note: An additional sense concerns birds disappearing while pursued. Por is split visually at the edge with a lowered r, not a comma after po.

runs.text: cauſa dalgum monte, ou ſerra que eſtà dian-

lines.note: A mountain or ridge in front accounts for the disappearance. Diante continues below, and its small division mark is displaced downward.

runs.text: te principalmente ſe diz das gallinhas do

lines.note: The usage particularly concerns gallinhas do mato, wild birds; retain this description instead of imposing a precise modern species.

runs.text: mato. Item, No Ximo ſe diz de gente que

lines.note: The regional note extends the expression in Ximo to people. Ximo is a Japanese regional label inside Portuguese.

runs.text: ſe encobre, ou deſaparece com algum mon-

lines.note: Those people become hidden or disappear behind a mountain; this is the regional extension of the preceding bird sense.
Te completes monte, ending the terrain qualification. It is not a Japanese hand noun here.
Hikikudasu is drawing something downward. The following phrase states how the lowering is done.
Puxando porella explains that one lowers the object by pulling it; the fused porella spelling is retained.
Hikida is glossed as lame or limping, with koshihiki expressly preferred. The damaged F is still recoverable as an initial.
Hikidasu is extracting something by pulling outward, a compact literal compound definition.

runs.text: Premio, ou dadiua que dà peſ-

lines.note: Hikidemono is a reward or gift. The social relation of giver and recipient follows below.

runs.text: ſoa mais nobre, ou igual a outra.

lines.note: The giver is superior or equal to the recipient, a restriction in this particular gift definition.
Hikihada is thin tanned hide. Curtida qualifies the prepared leather, not a Japanese inflection.
Hikiha denotes the time or opportunity to break camp; conjunção here expresses occasion.
O arrayal completes the camp-breaking gloss and identifies what is raised or abandoned.
Hikihagu means stripping skin or clothing away. The aida ending agrees with the voiced g-series of hagu.
Hikihanatsu is detaching or separating. The second Portuguese infinitive is divided apartar.
Partar completes apartar; this is not a new entry or omitted Japanese word.
Hikihanaruru is separating oneself, in contrast with the transitive hanatsu/hanasu entries nearby.
Hikihanasu returns to the transitive meaning of separating or detaching something.
Hikiharu means stretching taut by pulling, as confirmed by the bow example. An OCR t in the headword obscured haru.
Yumi o hisashiku hikihatte ireba describes keeping a bow drawn or strung for a long time. The consequence comes in the next row.
Yunzei tsukuru means the bow's strength is exhausted. The Portuguese bow context and visible initial y support yunjei rather than xunjei.
A bow left strung loses tension. Item then introduces another hikiharu use rather than continuing the bow example.

runs.text: Querer comprar de hũa parte, & de outra al

lines.note: Two sides both want to buy the same thing, described figuratively as pulling from opposite directions.

runs.text: gũa couſa como quem puxa por cada parte.

lines.note: The comparison with each side pulling completes that competing-purchasers explanation.
Hikihatakeru is opening or spreading something out. The examples below specify limbs and objects.
Shusoku o hiki hatakuru means opening out hands and feet, with shusoku as the paired limb noun.
Hands and feet finish the first example. Ki no yeda starts the next, concerning branches.
Branches and bunmawashi, a compass, are spread open. The infinitive ends quru, not the OCR quiu.

runs.text: der, & a largar ramos de aruore, abrir o com

lines.note: Spreading branches and opening a compass translate those two Japanese objects. Keep the visibly separated a largar.
Passo completes compasso, the drawing instrument, not a step in this context.
Hikihazusu means dislodging something from its fitted position. Its zzu spelling is preserved in the diplomatic text.

runs.text: ſa de ſeu lugar como pee de banco, deſarmar pa-

lines.note: A bench leg or dismantled hangings illustrates the removal. Pee is the visibly doubled-vowel word for foot.
Panos darmar completes the furnishings example. Permet introduces a figurative extension rather than a separate Japanese word.

runs.text: Apartarſe, ou eſcapulirſe de algũa par-

lines.note: Separating oneself or slipping away from a place supplies that figurative sense.
Te finishes parte, completing the departure-from-a-place gloss.
Hikihiraku means opening with force or by pulling. Both the initial F and the internal fi need recovery from faint print.
Ou puxando finishes the explanation of how the opening is accomplished; the bottom rule is visible beneath this row.
Hikihirogeru is opening or extending something broadly, related to hiroi rather than the previous hiraku compound.
Hiki hokorobakasu describes pulling stitching apart. Des begins the Portuguese descoſer over the row break.
Unsewing garments completes the preceding verb's definition. Coſer supplies the sewing component of descoſer.
Hikifuseru is throwing or pulling something down. The destination follows below.
No chaõ specifies the ground as the destination. Preserve the tilde carrier rather than normalizing to modern chão.

Hikigairu is given the synonym Vacufiqi and the unusual gloss Manduco. The animal-like headword is recognizable, but the local synonym and Portuguese label remain uncertain; preserve them rather than inventing an explanation.

runs.text: Pao com que fazem andar à roda,

lines.note: Hikigi is a wooden handle used to rotate something, identified as a millstone in the continuation.

runs.text: a mò de moer cha, farinha, &c.

lines.note: A mò is the millstone for grinding tea or flour. The feminine article is visible and matches mò; cha is Japanese-derived material within the gloss.

runs.text: Hũa laya de verruma grande de que

lines.note: Hikigiri is a large boring tool. The g in giri is important, distinguishing it from a cutting compound.
Ship carpenters use this large auger. The Portuguese relative clause completes the tool definition.
Hikigusu is taking people along with oneself. The headword's suru/ita sequence gives the verb's inflectional information.
Hito o hikigusuru explicitly illustrates bringing a person along; the whole phrase is Japanese after Vt.
Hikiidasu is pulling something out. The double i records the compound boundary and must not be collapsed to hikidasu merely because both entries exist.

runs.text: Gente que ſe vai retirando, ou aco-

lines.note: Hikizei denotes retreating personnel or forces; zei is the group element rather than a Portuguese syllable.
Acolhendo completes the withdrawing sense applied to the people above.
Hikiireru is drawing someone or something inside. The two adjacent i types correspond to hiki plus ire, repaired from OCR omission.
Hito o akudō ni hiki iruru is leading someone onto an evil path. The compound's segmentation is explicit in the example.

runs.text: peccados, ou no caminho da maldade.

lines.note: Sins or the path of wickedness explains akudō in this figurative application.

runs.text: Meter dentro na fortaleza a alguem

lines.note: Hiki ire is bringing someone inside a fortress, with a treacherous qualification on the next line.

runs.text: por traição, ou na caſa pera furtar. ¶

lines.note: The entry includes admitting someone by betrayal or admitting a thief into a house. Fi- starts its suru example.
The printed Fiquireuo ſuru is retained even though the surrounding entry favours hikiire; the line visibly lacks the expected extra i. The meaning is admission in this treacherous manner.

runs.text: Moſtra de ſe querer retirar, ou a-

lines.note: Hikiiro is an appearance or indication of retreat. The compound hiki plus iro explains the adjacent i types missed by OCR.
Hikiiro ni natta or hikiiro ni miyeta means becoming or appearing ready to withdraw. Both examples require the same iro element.

runs.text: Mostrarem os inimigos geito de ſe

lines.note: The enemies show signs of retreat; inimigos is the Portuguese noun, repaired from an m/n confusion.
Retirarem completes the appearance-of-retreat gloss, not a separate instruction.
Hikiiru is labelled a defective verb and illustrated with an army. Preserve this historical form rather than replacing it with modern hikiiru spelling conventions.
Commanding, directing and managing explain the military leadership verb. Iru continues the Japanese example from above.
O exercito is the object of those leadership verbs, completing the gloss.
Hikimadowasu is leading astray. Madouaxi is a continuous compound element, not ma followed by a separate word.

runs.text: zer errar o caminho. ¶ Item, Permet. Fa

lines.note: Misleading someone's route is extended figuratively by Permet. The next fazer begins at the row end.

runs.text: zer errar a alguem no caminho da ſaluação, ſci

lines.note: One can lead another astray in salvation or learning. Sci- belongs to sciencias below.
Sciencias completes the domains in which misleading guidance may occur.
Hikimaku is wrapping or tying. Emburilhar is preserved as printed, rather than silently reordered to modern embrulhar.
Girding oneself illustrates the wrapping action; cingindo-se clarifies how the object is wound around.
Hikimawaru is going round while pulling or leading. The visible m must not become ni in the kana reading.
Taking someone along completes the second manner of going round.

runs.text: Certa laya de ſerra de carpinteiro.

lines.note: Hikimawashi is a carpenter's saw in this entry. Serra is the tool noun; ferra was a meaning-changing long-s error.

runs.text: Fauor que ſe faz a algum hoſpede

lines.note: The next hikimawashi means assistance to a guest. Hospede is recognizable despite the OCR b/o errors.
Guiding and instructing the guest explain the assistance sense, distinct from the saw noun.
Hikimawasu is making something turn or go round by pulling. The verb's literal example follows.
Uma o hikimawasu is leading a horse round. Ro- starts rodear in the Portuguese repetition.

runs.text: dear o caualo. ¶ Item, Fauorecer, ou en-

lines.note: Rodear o cavalo completes that example. Item introduces helping or directing someone as a figurative extension.

runs.text: caminhar, & inſtruir a alguem que não ſabe ẽ

lines.note: The person lacks knowledge in some affairs, and receives direction or instruction. The final ẽ abbreviates the preposition.
Negocios completes the domain of assistance, meaning affairs or dealings rather than necessarily modern commerce.

runs.text: Hũa certa laya de frechas a ma-

lines.note: Hikime denotes a type of arrow. Its shape and use are explained in the next two lines.

runs.text: neira de rocas, dentro das quais metem cartas q̃

lines.note: The arrows are compared to distaffs and contain letters inside. Preserve the source's quais spelling and abbreviated q̃.
The letter-carrying arrows are shot toward the enemy side. The following Fiqi is separate page furniture.
